provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype override, licensed trade. Recurring plans against heavy big-brand advertising, so copy leans on local technicians and plain prep instructions. No product, chemical or brand names, no safety or health promises; licence numbers stay as bracketed placeholders. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pests by season in this area
pageStructurePlus.contains: A month-by-month calendar of the ants, roaches, spiders, wasps, mosquitoes, rodents and termites the technicians see locally, with the treatment visit each one calls for
pageStructurePlus.why: People search the bug, not the company. A seasonal pest page matches what they found in the kitchen to a visit they can book.

pageStructurePlus.section: Termite inspections and real estate reports
pageStructurePlus.contains: What a termite inspection looks at, the report format for home sales, bait versus liquid treatment explained in plain words, and how renewals and re-inspections work
pageStructurePlus.why: Termite work is the biggest ticket in pest control and the one buyers research hardest. Realtors and buyers need the report process spelled out.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Finding and sealing entry points, trapping, follow-up visits, attic insulation cleanup, and a written list of what was sealed
pageStructurePlus.why: Mouse and rat customers want them gone and kept out. Showing the sealing work separates real exclusion from a box of traps.

pageStructurePlus.section: Preparing for a treatment with kids and pets
pageStructurePlus.contains: What to move, cover or put away before the visit, when people and pets can go back into treated rooms according to the label, and who to call with a question
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents and pet owners hesitate at this exact step. Plain prep instructions, without promises, remove the reason they put the booking off.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What happens if pests come back between scheduled visits, how to request a free re-service, response times the owner commits to, and what the plan covers
pageStructurePlus.why: Plan customers cancel when bugs come back and nobody returns. A written re-service policy answers that fear before they sign up.

openers.line: Your Google listing has strong pest control reviews and no Website button, so someone who just saw ants marching across the counter can't see a plan price or book a visit.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where that ant search could land instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, where your quarterly pest plan is mentioned once in a post from spring. Plan buyers want the price and what's covered in one place.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and whether any plan details are visible.
openers.linkLine: Your pest plans and what they cover, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with a pest list from years ago and a form that bounces. Families comparing exterminators read that as a company that may not call back.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken thing: a dead form, an old number, a builder banner. Note it.
openers.linkLine: The same exterminator, with a form that books: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your pest control site cut off the booking form on my phone. People look for an exterminator with a flashlight in one hand and a phone in the other.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Pest control, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no price for a first pest treatment or a quarterly plan anywhere online, so the shopper picks the national brand ad with a number on it.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a published visit or plan price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A first-visit pest price and plan options: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts of termite tubes and damaged sill plates are exactly what a nervous homeowner needs to see, and they sink under the feed in a week.
openers.hook: Find one termite, rodent or wasp nest post and name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A termite and pest gallery that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews name the technician who explained everything and came back when the roaches did. That's what makes a pest plan feel safe, and it belongs beside the Book button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase that names a tech or a re-service. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pest reviews next to the plan sign-up: {demo-link}

openers.line: Termite swarmers and ant trails show up with the first warm days, and the calls come all at once. A booking page with open inspection slots catches the ones who won't leave a voicemail.
openers.hook: Use from February to May. Check for a post about swarmers or ants.

openers.line: When the nights get cold, mice move into attics and garages, and people search 'rodent control' at midnight after hearing scratching. That's the moment a booking page wins.
openers.hook: Use from September to December. Look for rodent or exclusion work in their posts.
openers.linkLine: Rodent control booked the night they hear it: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a pest control technician. Good applicants check whether the company looks steady before they train for the licence with you.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the truck. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A pest company page with a technician hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your pest reviews come from {Neighborhood} and nearby towns, but nothing online says where your routes run, so people one town over call a national brand instead.
openers.hook: Find the furthest town named in their reviews or posts and use it.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for your pest control routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: A termite treatment is a big bill nobody planned for. If you offer payments or monthly plans for it, saying so on the termite page keeps people from waiting another season.
openers.hook: Only if they mention payment plans or monthly billing anywhere. Never name a lender.
openers.linkLine: Termite treatment with payment options explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Treating inside someone's home is a trust decision. If you're state-licensed and insured, the licence belongs in writing beside the pest control price.
openers.hook: Look for a licence number or 'licensed and insured' on their listing, truck or posts. Use only what they publish, in [brackets] on the demo.
openers.linkLine: Licence and insurance on one pest page: {demo-link}

openers.line: When a neighbour posts 'who do you use for pest control', your name comes up over the national brands. The person who asked then looks you up and finds only a number.
openers.hook: Search their name in local Facebook groups or Nextdoor and find one recommendation. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a recommended exterminator should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your {specific recent job} post is the kind of pest problem people panic about. It deserves a page that explains the treatment and lets the next homeowner book.
openers.hook: Pick their newest pest post and name it: the wasp nest, the termite damage, the attic.
openers.linkLine: That pest job on a page that books: {demo-link}

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:

IF NO:

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a pest company your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}. A few new quarterly plans cover it in a year."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, after your route?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: The big brands outspend me everywhere.
objections.handler: "You won't outspend them, and you don't need to. When a family compares, the local exterminator with a named technician, a clear plan price and real reviews looks like the safer call. The site is where they compare."

objections.objection: I can't put prices online, every house is different.
objections.handler: "Show a starting price for the first treatment and the quarterly plan, and say termites and rodents are quoted after an inspection. That's honest and it stops the calls that only wanted a number."

objections.objection: My customers stay on the plan for years anyway.
objections.handler: "That's the point. Every new plan customer is worth years of pest visits, so the site only needs to win a few to pay for itself."

objections.objection: I'm worried about saying the wrong thing about chemicals.
objections.handler: "So am I. The site says nothing beyond your label instructions and your own prep sheet, and you approve every word. No safety promises, ever."

objections.objection: I already get leads from an app.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several pest companies at once. A plan customer who finds your own site signs up with you, and you don't pay per lead."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's plan pricing, booking, the termite page and the prep page. A few new quarterly pest plans cover it."

email.subject: Pest control site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for pest control companies in {City}, and I made a sample site for {Business Name} with plan prices and online booking. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} pest control demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — rodent season is starting in {City}, and people search for help the night they hear scratching in the attic. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to the yearly value of a few quarterly plans, never to one first treatment.
Plan sign-up and first-treatment booking are the core. Price termite, rodent and prep pages around them.
Price the termite page highest; it serves the biggest tickets and the real estate reports.
Every line about products or safety comes from the label and the owner's own sheet, and the owner signs it off; charge for that review time.
Never write a licence or certification the prospect hasn't published; leave a bracketed slot.
Keep monthly add-ons below one plan visit, so they never compete with a customer.

lineItems.item: Plan sign-up with first treatment booking
lineItems.description: Max with plan comparison, home size questions, card on file for recurring billing and a booked first visit.
Max with a real estate request form, closing-date field, sample report layout and renewal terms explained.
Max with an entry-point diagram, follow-up visit schedule and attic cleanup add-on request.
Max with printable sheets per treatment type, written from the owner's instructions and label directions and approved by them.
Max with a pest-by-month calendar for the area and a booking link per pest.
Max with restaurant, warehouse and property manager sections, service logs on request and a walkthrough form.
Max when each page names the neighbourhoods and the pests most asked about in that town.

whatElseYouSell.name: Plan conversion campaign for one-time treatments
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Everyone who books a one-time ant or roach treatment gets a friendly note a few weeks later offering the quarterly pest plan with that visit credited."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once one-time treatments come through the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with pest finds
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A real wasp nest, termite tube or sealed entry point on your Google profile every week, so the listing looks like a working exterminator."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each treatment
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A few days after each pest visit, a short note asks whether the problem is gone and invites a review, or a free re-service request first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring termite and autumn rodent campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two campaigns a year to past customers and their streets: termite inspections when swarmers appear and rodent exclusion when nights turn cold."

whatElseYouSell.name: Realtor termite report sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page termite inspection sheet for agents, with turnaround times and how to request a report, so they send closings to you."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck lettering and yard sign artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small yard sign after each pest treatment and lettering on the truck, with the plan sign-up address, so the street knows a local exterminator is nearby."

whatElseYouSell.name: Spanish version of the plan and prep pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Plan prices, prep sheets and the booking page in Spanish too, approved by the owner, for customers who'd rather read pest instructions in their language."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if their customers or technicians speak Spanish.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who refer termite work
withoutAI.whoPays: The inspector, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The buyers' inspector who hands you termite work on closings runs their own scheduling from a cell number. A small booking site for them is quick for me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors run small shops, need sites and trust the pest company they send work to.

withoutAI.whoPays: The wildlife company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your rodent customers have raccoons or bats, who do you send them to? That wildlife company needs an urgent-request page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wildlife and pest companies hand each other jobs constantly, so the introduction is natural.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The restaurant you treat every month has a menu stuck in a PDF. Your pest technician sees the owner more often than anyone."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Restaurant owners trust vendors who keep them inspection-ready, and they all need better sites.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The property manager who calls you for roach complaints between tenants still takes maintenance requests by email. A tenant request page is my next build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the exterminator who solves tenant complaints fast, and that trust gets a meeting.

withoutAI.route: Lawn care companies on the same streets
withoutAI.whoPays: The lawn care company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The lawn crew servicing your pest plan houses sells mowing by phone. Same recurring-plan layout, different service."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Both sell recurring plans to the same homeowners and swap referrals easily.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The attic contractor who replaces insulation after your rodent exclusions shows nothing online. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Attic jobs are bigger tickets, and the contractor relies on the pest company for referrals.

withAI.pitchLine: "Inspectors talk through each room and get a draft report, with possible termite and pest items flagged for a licensed specialist."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors write reports nightly, and every termite flag becomes a referral for the client.

withAI.pitchLine: "Callers describe the noise in the attic, and the assistant sorts likely rodent jobs for the pest company from raccoon and bat jobs for wildlife."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both businesses get cleaner calls, and the pest client gets the rodent work back.

withAI.pitchLine: "The kitchen manager asks what the last pest service found and when the next is, and the assistant answers from the service log ahead of an inspection."
withAI.whyItWorks: Restaurants dread inspections, and the pest client is already writing the log.

withAI.route: Tenant complaint sorter for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenant messages about bugs or mice get sorted by unit and urgency, and the exterminator gets the work order before the manager reads it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers spend mornings forwarding complaints; cutting that is easy to justify.

withAI.route: Lawn plan quote helper for the lawn company
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners enter their address and yard size, and the lawn crew gets a draft plan quote, the same flow I built for the pest plan sign-up."
withAI.whyItWorks: Already working for a business the lawn company trusts, so the pitch is short.

withAI.route: Attic job estimator for insulation contractors
withAI.pitchLine: "The pest technician's attic photos after a rodent exclusion become a draft insulation estimate the contractor can send the same day."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both companies win the same attic, and the handoff is already happening by text.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with plan prices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You're under a crawlspace and miss the call. The caller gets a text with your pest plan prices and a booking link within a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Visit-day text with prep reminder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day before each pest treatment, the customer gets the prep sheet for that service and a reminder to unlock the gate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the calendar and the owner-approved prep sheets.

softwareAI.name: Plan customer portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers see their next pest visit, past service notes and a re-service button, and update their card without calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the plan customer list and billing setup.

softwareAI.name: Booking chat for 'what's this bug' questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you treat carpenter ants' and 'what does the plan cover' from your own pest service list, then books the visit, and never gives safety advice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the service list, plan terms and calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for pest visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A customer thanks the tech for clearing the wasp nest; a reply in your voice naming that pest job is waiting in the van."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Service log with photos and products used
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Technicians log each pest treatment with areas treated, products, amounts and photos, ready for the customer, the state record and the next visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their current paper log and state record-keeping rules.

softwareAI.name: Bug photo identifier for incoming requests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers send a picture of the bug, and the technician gets a likely pest and a suggested visit type to confirm before calling back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past requests with photos and the pest that turned out to be. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Termite renewal tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every termite customer's renewal date, inspection history and bait station checks, with renewals sent before the coverage lapses."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their termite customer list and renewal terms.

softwareAI.name: After-hours receptionist for pest emergencies
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls at night about wasps by the front door or mice in the kitchen, and the receptionist takes the details and books the first exterminator slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the calendar, services and the owner's approved urgent-call wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Route planner for quarterly plan visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Quarterly pest visits grouped by neighbourhood and week, so each technician's day is tight and nobody misses a plan customer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs plan addresses, visit lengths and technician list.

softwareAI.name: Technician applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for pest technician jobs answer questions about licensing, driving and crawlspaces, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they're hiring. Needs must-haves, pay and training plan. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Re-service request follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a plan customer asks for a re-service, they get a time slot back right away and a check-in a week later asking if the pests are gone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the portal. Needs the re-service policy and calendar.

softwareAI.name: Commercial account service records
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Restaurants and warehouses download their pest service records and trap maps before an inspection, without calling the office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once they hold a few commercial accounts. Needs the service log.

softwareAI.name: Customer message sorter for pest jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Re-service requests, reschedules and 'are the ants supposed to be back' messages get sorted and drafted for the owner to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the business text line or inbox. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per plan route
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which pest plans and neighbourhoods make money once drive time, product and re-services are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a few months of service logs and product costs.

softwareAI.name: Termite inspection report drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The inspector talks through the crawlspace and attic, and a draft termite report with findings and photos is ready for the licensed inspector to check and sign."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past reports and the required report format. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plan cancellation save note
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a plan customer cancels, they get a polite note offering a free re-service first, and the owner sees why they left."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the cancellation flow and an offer the owner is happy to make.

softwareAI.name: Technician knowledge base from the owner's procedures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new technician asks how the owner handles a German roach job or a crawlspace entry, and gets the owner's written pest procedure, not a guess."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs written procedures and the owner's approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Realtor termite request board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Agents request a termite inspection for a listing, see when it's scheduled and download the report the moment it's signed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once agents order reports through the site. Needs agent contacts and the report workflow.

softwareAI.name: Bait station check map
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each property's termite and rodent stations on a simple map, with check dates and findings, so a new tech finds every station."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs station locations for current accounts.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the plan portal for independent pest companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Pest control companies, monthly per account
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a plan portal for one independent exterminator. Every small pest company loses plan customers who can't reach anyone for a re-service."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the re-service and billing workflow, which every plan-based pest company shares.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License plan sign-up and service logs to a pest supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every independent pest operator who buys from you a plan sign-up page and a service log, and they keep ordering through you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors compete for small operators, and a daily tool beats a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a site template with plan pricing, prep sheets and a licence slot, written to avoid the safety claims regulators dislike."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations care about compliant marketing and need member benefits; one agreement reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The acquiring group, per acquired brand
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each exterminator you acquire keeps its local name. One termite page, one plan sign-up and one portal template across all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roll-ups buy local brands and need them rebuilt fast and consistently.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label pest control template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency builds pest sites from scratch and risks a bad safety claim. License my template with approved prep pages and plan pricing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell the compliant, already-built part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Real estate brokerages' termite report desk
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every listing that needs a termite inspection gets ordered, tracked and filed from one desk, with vetted local inspectors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages chase reports on every closing and pay to stop the phone tag.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Apartment operators' pest work order board
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every unit's pest complaints, treatments and follow-ups on one board across all your properties, with service records for audits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Operators juggle pest complaints constantly and need records; the exterminator client already makes them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pest service records, trap maps and corrective actions for every location in one place before the health inspector arrives."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups with several kitchens need consistent records, and the pest client already produces them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same pest control stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New pest clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one independent exterminator per area, and {City} has one. The neighbouring county is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the plan pages, the prep sheets and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home warranty companies' pest add-on vendors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members who add pest coverage get booked with vetted local exterminators from one page, with the service log attached to their account."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Warranty firms need reliable local vendors and records; independents need the volume.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Licensing exam prep for new technicians
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Pest companies or the training provider, per seat
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New pest technicians study for the state exam with practice questions built from the public study material, not guesses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every company trains new techs for the licence and hiring is their hardest problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue stalled pest company software builds
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Paid for a pest plan portal or service log that never shipped? I've finished that exact build for an exterminator already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy; they want someone who has finished one.
